rules.statement: Never put secret values (connection strings, keys, certificates) in Helm chart values; reference operator-created Kubernetes Secrets by name instead.
rules.why: Values files may be committed to public repositories, so no chart value may be a secret.
rules.check: Look for chart values or templates that accept a connection string, password, key or certificate inline rather than a Secret name/secretKeyRef.

rules.statement: Make a Helm chart fail at render time (e.g. with `fail`/`required`) for any configuration the application would refuse at startup or that cannot work safely, instead of deploying it.
rules.why: `helm install` then fails before anything is applied rather than leaving a pod in a crash loop.
rules.check: A new application startup validation or unsafe combination (wildcard allowed hosts, missing required Secret, multiple replicas without shared state) that has no matching render-time failure in the chart templates.

rules.statement: Give each Helm chart a `values.schema.json` that types every value and rejects unknown properties.
rules.why: A typo or mistyped value must fail instead of being silently ignored.
rules.check: New values added to values.yaml without a schema entry, or schema objects missing `additionalProperties: false`.

rules.statement: When replicas keep single-use state in-process without a shared store, use the `Recreate` deployment strategy and refuse more than one replica; use a rolling update with `maxSurge: 1`, `maxUnavailable: 0` only when state is shared.
rules.why: A rolling update, even with `maxSurge: 0`, starts the new pod while the old one may still be serving, so two replicas with separate single-use state would overlap.
rules.check: Deployment strategy templates that use RollingUpdate (including maxSurge: 0) when no shared state store is configured, or allow replicas > 1 without it.

rules.statement: Make chart pods meet the restricted Pod Security Standard: run as non-root UID, drop all capabilities, set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, use the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile, use a read-only root filesystem with an `emptyDir` for `/tmp`, and disable service-account token automount unless the app calls the Kubernetes API.
rules.why: The hardened image is meant to run with minimal privilege, and a host that never calls the Kubernetes API needs no token.
rules.check: Pod/container securityContext missing any of these settings, or `automountServiceAccountToken` not false for an app that does not use the Kubernetes API.

rules.statement: Mount Secrets that contain private keys with mode `0440` under an `fsGroup` matching the app's group.
rules.why: Only the application's group should be able to read the private key.
rules.check: Secret volumes for keys/certificates with default or broader `defaultMode`, or missing a matching `fsGroup`.

rules.statement: Point startup and liveness probes at a liveness endpoint that does not depend on external dependencies such as the database, and use the readiness endpoint only for readiness; when host filtering is enabled, send an explicit allowed, non-wildcard `Host` header from each probe.
rules.why: A lost database must not restart pods, and the kubelet's default Host (the pod IP) is rejected by AllowedHosts with 400.
rules.check: Liveness/startup probes hitting a readiness or dependency-checking endpoint, or httpGet probes without an httpHeaders Host entry when AllowedHosts is configured.

rules.statement: Give chart pods a `preStop` delay so a terminating pod keeps serving while the ingress removes it, followed by graceful shutdown within the termination grace period; use the kubelet `sleep` action rather than a shell command for shell-less images.
rules.why: Prevents dropped requests during rollout, and chiseled images have no shell to run `sleep`.
rules.check: Deployments without a preStop drain, preStop using `exec: sh -c sleep` for shell-less images, or a grace period shorter than drain plus shutdown time.

rules.statement: In chart CI, run `helm lint --strict`, render each supported example release, and assert that each unsafe release fails to render.
rules.why: CI checks the chart's contract, including that its refusals actually trigger.
rules.check: New render-time validation added without a matching CI case that expects rendering to fail.
